roles.label: Viewer
roles.description: Read-only access to everything, and subscribing yourself to the alarms you can see. The floor every other role inherits.

roles.label: Operator
roles.description: Day-to-day operations: create or edit components, endpoints (retry an endpoint's rejected session, or run its poll now), secrets, variables, the property, metric, event, command and notification catalogs, issue commands in scope, preview a driver spec through a node, and impair simulated devices. Sees and reveals the device secrets in its scope (never the admin-sensitive platform credentials). Inherits Viewer.

roles.label: Deploy
roles.description: Integrator or field tech: create, update, rename, and move on locations, systems, and components, and no delete. A grant of it reaches ONE tier, the tier it is scoped at. Granted at a location with the "under only" operator, it builds out and edits the rooms under that location, never the location itself, plus the secrets those locations own; it reaches no system and no component there, not even to read one. Building those out inside a building takes a system-scoped and a component-scoped grant of this role beside the location one, until a grant's scope can span tiers. Inherits Viewer, whose read floor is scoped the same way.

roles.label: Administrator
roles.description: Manages the fleet, users, roles, and grants: full create, update, and delete on locations, systems, and components, and on principals, credentials, grants, and roles. Deliberately NOT the superuser: it cannot grant a role above its own tier, so it cannot make itself owner. Inherits Operator.

roles.label: Owner
roles.description: Full control of everything, the break-glass superuser (the tail wildcard, so it covers every capability at every tier, including admin-sensitive ones and future resources). At least one active owner always exists, and an owner account cannot be impersonated.

property_types.name: icmp-reachable
property_types.label: ICMP Reachable
property_types.description: ICMP inline probe result: up when at least one echo returned, down when none did. A state, stored on transition only; icmp-rtt-avg carries the timing beside it.

property_types.name: tcp-open
property_types.label: TCP Port Open
property_types.description: TCP-connect probe result: open when the port accepted a connection, closed when it refused or timed out. A state, stored on transition only; tcp-connect-time carries the timing beside it.

property_types.name: endpoint-reachable
property_types.label: Endpoint Reachable
property_types.description: Per-endpoint reachability verdict, the AND of the endpoint's probe results (up = every applicable probe reached the target). A built-in state: availability is time_in_state over it. Unknown/stale are read-time derivations, not stored values.

property_types.name: endpoint-responsive
property_types.label: Endpoint Responsive
property_types.description: The layer-7 rung beside endpoint-reachable: the protocol itself answered (an HTTP request drew a response, an SSH exchange completed). A port that accepts but never answers is reachable and not responsive, which is the distinction this verdict exists to draw.

property_types.name: endpoint-authenticated
property_types.label: Endpoint Authenticated
property_types.description: The auth rung: the credential the probe carried was accepted. Written only when a credential was actually tried, so an unauthenticated probe never reads as a failed login.

property_types.name: session-state
property_types.label: Session State
property_types.description: A held session's state per endpoint: establishing (the first connection is being made), up (the connection is held and polls borrow it), recovering (a held connection dropped and the node is reconnecting with a bounded, jittered backoff), down (the attempt budget is spent; the node keeps retrying at the capped pace), rejected (a refusal retrying cannot fix, such as a wrong credential or a changed host key; the node dials no more until the endpoint changes or an operator retries). Written on transitions only; session-reason carries why.

property_types.name: session-reason
property_types.label: Session Reason
property_types.description: Why a held session is in its state: the reason of its latest transition. A rejected session's reason is its class and the component's own text (auth: auth rejected), so an event rule can alarm on it. Written beside session-state on every transition.

property_types.name: ssh-host-key
property_types.label: SSH Host Key
property_types.description: The SHA256 fingerprint of the host key an ssh session trusts, per endpoint. The node records the first key it sees (trust on first use) and every connection that matches it; a changed key is refused, and the session reads rejected with class host-key naming both fingerprints until an operator retries the endpoint with the new key, which lands here as the declared value.

property_types.name: tls-certificate
property_types.label: TLS Certificate Key
property_types.description: The SHA256 fingerprint of the public key a tls endpoint pins, per endpoint, in the form ssh fingerprints a host key in. In pin mode the node records the first key it is offered (trust on first use), and records it again while the server does not yet deliver it back as the pin; a renewal that keeps the key is no change, and a changed key is refused, the session reading rejected with class certificate naming both fingerprints, until an operator retries the endpoint with the new key, which lands here as the declared value.

property_types.name: tls-certificate-expiry
property_types.label: TLS Certificate Expiry
property_types.description: The not-after of the certificate a tls probe accepted (RFC 3339, UTC), per endpoint, stored on change. The days left beside it, tls-certificate-days-left, is the number a rule reads.

property_types.name: endpoint-rejection
property_types.label: Endpoint Rejection
property_types.description: An endpoint's gate: the ladder rung a refusal retrying cannot fix holds (responsive for a host key, certificate or protocol refusal, authenticated for a credential), its class, and the connection fingerprint it holds for, or none. While the fingerprint is unchanged nothing at or above that rung is attempted again; a changed secret, address, port, transport, login declaration or pin, or an operator's retry, lifts it. The fingerprint is a digest only. A refusal of a changed key (class host-key) appends its evidence, the pinned key and the key the component offered instead, each a SHA256 fingerprint. The gate is a set of reasons: beside that refusal, which comes first, each other reason is an entry of its kind, since when (RFC 3339) and the task that added it, the entries joined by a semicolon (unreachable 2026-11-09T14:03:00Z task-1, from the endpoint's own probe reading down twice in a row, lifted by its next up).

property_types.name: endpoint-rejection-reason
property_types.label: Endpoint Rejection Reason
property_types.description: Why an endpoint's gate holds: the refusal's class and the component's own text (auth: the agent answered authorizationError for the community), scrubbed by the node of anything it sent. Written beside endpoint-rejection whenever the node records a gate, held session or not, so an endpoint gated by its reachability probe alone still says why it was refused. A gate a restarted node adopts writes none, and the read serves the reason only while a gate holds.

property_types.name: health
property_types.label: Health
property_types.description: The rolled-up health verdict for a component, system, or location, worst-wins over its inputs (a component's active alarms, a system's roles, the systems under a location). Recorded transition-only, so the series is the edges: when it broke and when it came back, not a sample per check. incomplete ranks between healthy and degraded and means a commissioning gap: a role short because its hardware was never installed, which no alarm will ever fire for.

property_types.name: server-version
property_types.label: Server Version
property_types.description: The Omniglass build this server runs, written by its boot and rewritten when an upgrade changes it.

property_types.name: server-started-at
property_types.label: Server Started At
property_types.description: When this server last booted, an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp its boot writes; the server's uptime is the time since.

property_types.name: video-input
property_types.label: Video Input
property_types.description: The selected video input on a display or switcher. A settable state: the set-input command tells the device which input to select (opening an intended value), and the device reports the observed input, so the two reconcile.

property_types.name: power-state
property_types.label: Power State
property_types.description: Whether a component is on, off, or in standby. A settable state: the set-power command tells the component which to enter, and its report settles it.

property_types.name: outlet-1-state
property_types.label: Outlet 1 State
property_types.description: Whether the first outlet of a power conditioner is switched on or off, as the component reports it.

property_types.name: outlet-2-state
property_types.label: Outlet 2 State
property_types.description: Whether the second outlet of a power conditioner is switched on or off, as the component reports it.

property_types.name: outlet-3-state
property_types.label: Outlet 3 State
property_types.description: Whether the third outlet of a power conditioner is switched on or off, as the component reports it.

property_types.name: outlet-4-state
property_types.label: Outlet 4 State
property_types.description: Whether the fourth outlet of a power conditioner is switched on or off, as the component reports it.

property_types.name: mute
property_types.label: Mute
property_types.description: Whether a component's audio is muted, as the component reports it ("true" or "false"). A settable state: the set-mute command tells the component which.

property_types.name: call-state
property_types.label: Call State
property_types.description: Whether a conferencing component is in a call (active) or not (idle).

property_types.name: content-sharing-state
property_types.label: Content Sharing State
property_types.description: Whether a conferencing component is sharing content (a presentation) from a source or not (idle).

property_types.name: tracking-state
property_types.label: Tracking State
property_types.description: Whether a camera is following a presenter on its own (tracking) or holds where it was pointed (manual).

property_types.name: occupancy-state
property_types.label: Occupancy State
property_types.description: Whether a space reads occupied or vacant by its occupancy source.

property_types.name: shutter-state
property_types.label: Shutter State
property_types.description: Whether a projector's shutter is open (the image shows) or closed (the image is blanked with the light source still lit).

property_types.name: protect-state
property_types.label: Protect State
property_types.description: Whether an amplifier is running (normal) or has muted its outputs and latched protect on a fault (overheating, a shorted load, DC on an output), which holds until an operator resets it.

property_types.name: signal-state
property_types.label: Signal State
property_types.description: Whether a signal device detects a signal on the input it carries (a switcher's routed input, an extender's input), as it reports it.

property_types.name: link-state
property_types.label: Link State
property_types.description: Whether the link between a signal device and its far end (an extender's cable run to its transmitter) is up or down, as the device reports it.

property_types.name: playback-state
property_types.label: Playback State
property_types.description: Whether a media player is playing its content, paused on it, or stopped.

property_types.name: content-name
property_types.label: Content Name
property_types.description: The name of the item a media player is playing, as it reports it.

property_types.name: service-state
property_types.label: Service State
property_types.description: A software service's own account of its health, as its health endpoint reports it.

property_types.name: software-version
property_types.label: Software Version
property_types.description: The version of the software a service reports it is running.

property_types.name: booking-state
property_types.label: Booking State
property_types.description: Whether a space is booked now (a meeting in progress) or free, as its scheduling service reports it.

property_types.name: program-state
property_types.label: Program State
property_types.description: Whether a control processor is running its loaded program or has it stopped, as the processor reports it.

property_types.name: scene-state
property_types.label: Scene State
property_types.description: The current scene a room is in, as reported by a control panel or processor (idle, presentation, or video conference mode).

property_types.name: serial-number
property_types.label: Serial number
property_types.description: The manufacturer serial number of the device.

property_types.name: mac-address
property_types.label: MAC address
property_types.description: The primary hardware (MAC) address, lowercase colon-separated.

property_types.name: firmware-version
property_types.label: Firmware version
property_types.description: The installed firmware or software version.

property_types.name: model-number
property_types.label: Model number
property_types.description: The manufacturer model number.

property_types.name: ucc-room-id
property_types.label: UCC room id
property_types.description: The id a unified-communications service gives one of the rooms it reports on. A driver on the service's component reads it off each record, and an identity binding on that component ties each id to the system or component it names.

metric_types.name: icmp-rtt-avg
metric_types.label: ICMP RTT (avg)
metric_types.description: Average round-trip time over the task's echoes; absent when unreachable.

metric_types.name: tcp-connect-time
metric_types.label: TCP Connect Time
metric_types.description: Time to establish the TCP connection; absent when the port is closed.

metric_types.name: poll-duration
metric_types.label: Poll Duration
metric_types.description: Mean time of the endpoint's driver poll runs over the report window, scheduled or run now, answered or failed; absent when no poll ran.

metric_types.name: poll-failure-count
metric_types.label: Poll Failures
metric_types.description: The endpoint's driver polls that failed in the report window (faulted and landed nothing, or refused by the endpoint's gate); reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: poll-held-count
metric_types.label: Held Polls
metric_types.description: The endpoint's due driver polls its gate held in the report window because its probe reads it unreachable, a disruptive command (a reboot) holds it, or a component it is reached through is down (which holds its probes too, counted here); never sent, so not failures; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: hold-expiry-count
metric_types.label: Hold Expiries
metric_types.description: Disruptions of the endpoint (a reboot closed its gate) released in the report window by the command type's hold backstop because no up verdict came after the quiet period; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: poll-due-count
metric_types.label: Due Polls
metric_types.description: The endpoint's driver polls that fell due in the report window, each on its own interval, held, refused and skipped ones included; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: poll-skipped-count
metric_types.label: Skipped Polls
metric_types.description: The endpoint's due driver polls the node skipped in the report window because the poll's last run was still in flight; counted, never queued; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: push-message-count
metric_types.label: Pushed Messages
metric_types.description: Messages the endpoint's held session or udp socket delivered that a listener claimed in the report window; zero when quiet.

metric_types.name: push-unclaimed-count
metric_types.label: Unclaimed Messages
metric_types.description: Messages the endpoint delivered that no listener claimed in the report window; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: webhook-post-count
metric_types.label: Webhook Posts
metric_types.description: Webhook posts to the endpoint the server accepted in the report window; one zero follows a window with posts, then none while quiet.

metric_types.name: webhook-refusal-count
metric_types.label: Webhook Refusals
metric_types.description: Webhook posts to the endpoint the server refused (a bad signature, a missing credential) in the report window; reported only when nonzero.

metric_types.name: checkin-age
metric_types.label: Check-in Age
metric_types.description: Seconds since the node's last heartbeat reached the server (since its enrollment, before its first), written by the server every platform tick; keeps growing while the node is silent.

metric_types.name: worklist-task-count
metric_types.label: Worklist Tasks
metric_types.description: Tasks in the worklist the node installed, sampled on each install.

metric_types.name: tick-duration
metric_types.label: Tick Duration
metric_types.description: The longest pass the node's dispatcher took over one heartbeat window, sampled each heartbeat.

metric_types.name: tick-overrun-count
metric_types.label: Tick Overruns
metric_types.description: Dues that met their task's previous run still in flight, so were skipped, over the report window; reported every window, 0 when quiet.

metric_types.name: schedule-lateness
metric_types.label: Schedule Lateness
metric_types.description: The worst gap between a task's due time and its dispatch over one heartbeat window's scheduled runs.

metric_types.name: schedule-gap-excess
metric_types.label: Schedule Gap Excess
metric_types.description: The worst deviation between a task's gap since its previous scheduled start and its interval over one heartbeat window; a poll keeping its interval reads 0, a skipped slot a whole interval.

metric_types.name: schedule-skip-count
metric_types.label: Schedule Skips
metric_types.description: Task dues the dispatcher passed over (a run still in flight, a late pass), over the report window; reported every window, 0 when quiet.

metric_types.name: spool-batch-count
metric_types.label: Spool Depth
metric_types.description: Batches waiting in the node's spool for the bus, sampled each tick.

metric_types.name: delivery-in-count
metric_types.label: Delivery In
metric_types.description: Items that reached a hop over the report window, one sample per kind as the instance (metric, property, event, log); a node counts its spool, the server its ingest. At a node's schedule/{kind} instance it counts the runs due on the schedule that produce that kind. Written every window, 0 when quiet.

metric_types.name: delivery-out-count
metric_types.label: Delivery Out
metric_types.description: Items a hop handed on over the report window, one sample per kind as the instance (metric, property, event, log); a node counts what the bus acknowledged, the server what it stored, coalesced, or had already landed. At a node's schedule/{kind} instance it counts the runs made of those due. Written every window, 0 when quiet.

metric_types.name: delivery-loss-ratio
metric_types.label: Delivery Loss
metric_types.description: The share of a hop's items that came in and never went out over the report window, one sample per kind as the instance (metric, property, event, log); at a node's schedule/{kind} instance, the share of runs due that were skipped. 0 is healthy, and a quiet window writes 0.

metric_types.name: session-held-count
metric_types.label: Sessions Held
metric_types.description: Device sessions the node holds, one sample per session state as the instance, sampled each tick.

metric_types.name: process-goroutine-count
metric_types.label: Goroutines
metric_types.description: Goroutines the Omniglass process runs, sampled each tick.

metric_types.name: process-heap-size
metric_types.label: Heap Size
metric_types.description: Bytes of heap the Omniglass process holds in live and unswept objects, sampled each tick.

metric_types.name: process-gc-pause
metric_types.label: GC Pause
metric_types.description: The most recent garbage collection pause of the Omniglass process; absent until the first collection.

metric_types.name: process-cpu-seconds
metric_types.label: CPU Time
metric_types.description: CPU time the Omniglass process spent since its previous sample (each tick on a node, each report window on the server), as the Go runtime estimates it rather than the kernel's account; divided by that interval it is the cores the process kept busy.

metric_types.name: process-fd-count
metric_types.label: Open Files
metric_types.description: File descriptors the Omniglass process holds open, sockets included; absent where the platform does not expose them.

metric_types.name: retention-deleted-count
metric_types.label: Retention Deleted
metric_types.description: Rows the retention pass removed from one lane in one pass; a day's partition dropped whole is counted in Metric Partitions Dropped, not here.

metric_types.name: retention-behind
metric_types.label: Retention Behind
metric_types.description: 1 when the pass stopped at its chunk cap with rows (or compaction work) still past the window, or its prune or compaction failed, 0 when it caught up; a lane that stays at 1 is falling behind.

metric_types.name: retention-pass-duration
metric_types.label: Retention Pass Duration
metric_types.description: Wall time of one retention pass, every lane, the partition roll and both compactions.

metric_types.name: retention-pass-failure-count
metric_types.label: Retention Pass Failures
metric_types.description: Steps of one retention pass that returned an error (a lane, the roll, a compaction, a window out of range); 0 on a clean pass.

metric_types.name: retention-window-days
metric_types.label: Retention Window
metric_types.description: The retention window in days the pass applied to a lane.

metric_types.name: metric-partition-created-count
metric_types.label: Metric Partitions Created
metric_types.description: Day partitions of the metric table the pass created ahead of now.

metric_types.name: metric-partition-dropped-count
metric_types.label: Metric Partitions Dropped
metric_types.description: Day partitions of the metric table the pass dropped whole, every row in them past the window.

metric_types.name: metric-partition-count
metric_types.label: Metric Partitions
metric_types.description: Day partitions the metric table holds after the pass.

metric_types.name: metric-oldest-day-age
metric_types.label: Oldest Metric Day
metric_types.description: Days from the start of the oldest metric partition to the pass; steady at about the metric window plus one once retention keeps up.

metric_types.name: metric-trend-mark-lag
metric_types.label: Trend Compaction Lag
metric_types.description: Hours from the trend compaction's mark to now; steady at about 24 to 25, the trend horizon, and growing when the compaction falls behind.

metric_types.name: metric-block-mark-lag
metric_types.label: Block Compaction Lag
metric_types.description: Days from the block fold's mark to now; steady at about 1 to 2 (a day folds once its hours are compacted) and growing when the fold falls behind.

metric_types.name: table-bytes
metric_types.label: Table Size
metric_types.description: On-disk bytes of one stored table with its indexes and toast; the metric table's is the sum of its day partitions.

metric_types.name: database-bytes
metric_types.label: Database Size
metric_types.description: On-disk bytes of the whole Omniglass database.

metric_types.name: http-request-count
metric_types.label: HTTP Requests
metric_types.description: Requests the server answered for one method, route template and status class over the report window; one zero follows a window with requests, then none while quiet.

metric_types.name: http-request-duration
metric_types.label: HTTP Request Time
metric_types.description: Mean time the server took to answer a request of one method, route template and status class over the report window.

metric_types.name: http-request-duration-max
metric_types.label: HTTP Request Time (max)
metric_types.description: The slowest request of one method, route template and status class over the report window.

metric_types.name: db-slow-query-count
metric_types.label: Slow Queries
metric_types.description: Queries that ran past the database slow-query threshold over the report window, each also logged as a warning with its fingerprint; one zero follows a window with slow queries.

metric_types.name: db-pool-acquired
metric_types.label: Pool Connections In Use
metric_types.description: Database connections the server's pool had checked out at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: db-pool-idle
metric_types.label: Pool Connections Idle
metric_types.description: Open database connections the server's pool held idle at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: db-pool-total
metric_types.label: Pool Connections Open
metric_types.description: Database connections the server's pool held open, in use or idle, at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: db-pool-max
metric_types.label: Pool Size
metric_types.description: The most connections the server's pool may open; db-pool-total reaching it means a new query waits.

metric_types.name: db-pool-wait-count
metric_types.label: Pool Waits
metric_types.description: Connection acquires that found the pool exhausted and waited for a connection, over the report window.

metric_types.name: db-pool-wait-duration
metric_types.label: Pool Wait Time
metric_types.description: Total time acquires spent waiting on an exhausted pool for a connection to free up or open, over the report window.

metric_types.name: ingest-lag
metric_types.label: Ingest Lag
metric_types.description: Mean time from a sample's timestamp to its batch's commit on the server, over the newest and oldest sample of each batch landed in the report window; the node's clock stamps the sample, so a skewed node clock reads as lag.

metric_types.name: ingest-lag-max
metric_types.label: Ingest Lag (max)
metric_types.description: The oldest sample's lag at commit across every batch landed in the report window.

metric_types.name: ingest-batch-count
metric_types.label: Batches Landed
metric_types.description: Telemetry batches the server committed over the report window; a redelivery its receipt held to a no-op landed nothing and counts none.

metric_types.name: ingest-sample-count
metric_types.label: Samples Landed
metric_types.description: Samples the server's committed telemetry batches landed over the report window; a node group the fence or the gateway dropped counts none.

metric_types.name: ingest-lane-busy
metric_types.label: Ingest Lane Busy
metric_types.description: Share of the report window the telemetry lane spent handling batches; near 1 the lane is saturated and the consumer backlog grows.

metric_types.name: bus-consumer-pending
metric_types.label: Telemetry Backlog
metric_types.description: Batches on the telemetry stream not yet delivered to the server's consumer, at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: bus-consumer-ack-pending
metric_types.label: Telemetry In Flight
metric_types.description: Batches delivered to the server's telemetry consumer and not yet acknowledged, at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: bus-consumer-redelivered
metric_types.label: Telemetry Redelivering
metric_types.description: Batches the telemetry consumer holds that were delivered more than once, at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: bus-consumer-ack-floor
metric_types.label: Telemetry Ack Floor
metric_types.description: The telemetry stream sequence at and below which the server's consumer has answered every batch, landed or dropped, read at the report. It reaching an earlier bus-stream-last-seq proves every batch the stream held by then is settled, under any steady load.

metric_types.name: bus-stream-last-seq
metric_types.label: Telemetry Stream Head
metric_types.description: The sequence of the last batch the telemetry stream stored, read at the report; it only grows, so the batches published by a moment are all at or below the head read after it.

metric_types.name: bus-telemetry-ack-failure-count
metric_types.label: Telemetry Ack Failures
metric_types.description: Batch deliveries whose acknowledgement the bus did not confirm over the report window, a redelivery its receipt held included; each is redelivered and its receipt keeps it from landing twice, so this costs work, not rows. As a share of ingest-batch-count, healthy is 0.

metric_types.name: bus-worklist-pull-count
metric_types.label: Worklist Pulls
metric_types.description: Node worklist pulls the server answered over the report window, one sample per outcome as the instance (served, read-failed, oversize, respond-failed, expired, abandoned, busy).

metric_types.name: bus-worklist-reply-bytes-max
metric_types.label: Worklist Reply Size (max)
metric_types.description: The largest worklist reply the server holds sized for any node, at the end of the report window; nearing the bus payload limit means a reply will be refused as oversize.

metric_types.name: bus-request-count
metric_types.label: Bus Requests
metric_types.description: Node requests the server handled on the bus over the report window, one sample per path as the instance (heartbeat, command-pull, command-report).

metric_types.name: bus-request-failure-count
metric_types.label: Bus Request Failures
metric_types.description: Node requests on the bus the server failed to serve over the report window, one sample per path as the instance; a share of bus-request-count.

metric_types.name: calc-pending-depth
metric_types.label: Calc Backlog
metric_types.description: The deepest the queue of calculated metrics waiting to be computed stood over the report window.

metric_types.name: calc-served-count
metric_types.label: Calcs Served
metric_types.description: Calculated metric rows the server computed over the report window.

metric_types.name: calc-pass-duration
metric_types.label: Calc Pass Time
metric_types.description: Mean time one pass over the calc queue took over the report window.

metric_types.name: outbox-queued-depth
metric_types.label: Outbox Depth
metric_types.description: Notifications queued to send, due or waiting out a retry backoff, at the end of the report window.

metric_types.name: outbox-due-age
metric_types.label: Outbox Due Age
metric_types.description: How long the oldest due notification has waited past its send time, at the end of the report window; zero when nothing is due.

metric_types.name: sweep-duration
metric_types.label: Sweep Time
metric_types.description: Mean time one pass of a server sweep took over the report window, one sample per sweep as the instance (command-settlement, event-rule).

metric_types.name: sweep-count
metric_types.label: Sweeps
metric_types.description: Passes of a server sweep over the report window, one sample per sweep as the instance.

metric_types.name: sweep-failure-count
metric_types.label: Sweep Failures
metric_types.description: Passes of a server sweep that failed over the report window, one sample per sweep as the instance; a share of sweep-count.

metric_types.name: command-pending-count
metric_types.label: Pending Commands
metric_types.description: Commands waiting for the node, the ones its next pull would take and the ones it took that await their execution report, sampled each platform tick.

metric_types.name: command-pending-age
metric_types.label: Oldest Pending Command
metric_types.description: Seconds the oldest command waiting for the node has waited since its issue, sampled each platform tick; zero while none waits.

metric_types.name: command-dispatch-latency
metric_types.label: Command Dispatch Latency
metric_types.description: Time from a command's issue to the first time a node took it, one sample per command at that take; a command no node takes writes none and counts as expired.

metric_types.name: command-execution-latency
metric_types.label: Command Execution Latency
metric_types.description: Time from a command's first take to the node's execution report, one sample per command at the report.

metric_types.name: command-redelivery-count
metric_types.label: Command Redeliveries
metric_types.description: Commands a pull redelivered (taken again after no report came) over the platform tick's window, read 5 s behind the tick so a take still committing is not missed; written every tick, zero when none.

metric_types.name: command-stuck-count
metric_types.label: Stuck Commands
metric_types.description: Commands the node took that have had no execution report for longer than the redelivery wait, still inside the delivery window, sampled each platform tick.

metric_types.name: command-expired-count
metric_types.label: Expired Commands
metric_types.description: Commands that aged past the delivery window unexecuted over the platform tick's window, instance undelivered (no node took it) or unexecuted (taken, never reported); written every tick, zero when none.

metric_types.name: command-pull-failure-count
metric_types.label: Command Pull Failures
metric_types.description: Pulls of the node's command queue that failed (no answer, or one it could not read), over the report window; reported every window, 0 when quiet.

metric_types.name: room-temperature
metric_types.label: Room Temperature
metric_types.description: Ambient temperature reported for the space, in degrees Celsius.

metric_types.name: occupancy-count
metric_types.label: Occupancy Count
metric_types.description: People detected in the space by the room's occupancy source.

metric_types.name: booking-count
metric_types.label: Booking Count
metric_types.description: Meetings booked in the space for the rest of the day, the one in progress included, as its scheduling service reports them.

metric_types.name: uptime
metric_types.label: Uptime
metric_types.description: How long the device reports it has been running, in seconds (an SNMP sysUpTime scaled from timeticks, or the driver's equivalent).

metric_types.name: volume
metric_types.label: Volume
metric_types.description: The output volume a component reports, as a percentage of its range. A settable quantity: the set-volume command opens an intended volume and settles when the component reports it.

metric_types.name: participant-count
metric_types.label: Participant Count
metric_types.description: The participants a component reports in its current call; 0 when no call is active.

metric_types.name: audio-level
metric_types.label: Audio Level
metric_types.description: The audio level a component reports, in decibels relative to digital full scale (0 is the loudest it can carry).

metric_types.name: battery-charge
metric_types.label: Battery Charge
metric_types.description: How charged a component reports its battery, as a fraction of full (0 to 1).

metric_types.name: light-source-hours
metric_types.label: Light Source Hours
metric_types.description: The hours a component reports its light source (a projector's lamp or laser) has been lit.

metric_types.name: temperature
metric_types.label: Temperature
metric_types.description: The temperature a component reports of itself (its chassis, heatsink or processor), in degrees Celsius.

metric_types.name: fan-speed
metric_types.label: Fan Speed
metric_types.description: The speed a component reports of its cooling fan, in revolutions per minute.

metric_types.name: voltage
metric_types.label: Voltage
metric_types.description: The voltage a component reports at its input, in volts.

metric_types.name: current
metric_types.label: Current
metric_types.description: The total current a component reports drawing, in amperes.

metric_types.name: pan-angle
metric_types.label: Pan Angle
metric_types.description: How far a camera reports it is panned from its centre, in degrees (negative to the left, positive to the right).

metric_types.name: tilt-angle
metric_types.label: Tilt Angle
metric_types.description: How far a camera reports it is tilted from level, in degrees (negative down, positive up).

metric_types.name: zoom-level
metric_types.label: Zoom Level
metric_types.description: The magnification a camera reports, as a multiple of its widest view (1 is the widest).

metric_types.name: camera-preset
metric_types.label: Camera Preset
metric_types.description: The number of the stored position a camera reports it is on; 0 when it is on none (it was pointed by hand or is tracking).

metric_types.name: peripheral-count
metric_types.label: Peripheral Count
metric_types.description: How many peripherals (cameras, microphones, touch panels) a component reports attached to it.

metric_types.name: storage-utilization
metric_types.label: Storage Utilization
metric_types.description: How full a component reports its local storage, as a fraction of its capacity (0 to 1).

metric_types.name: active-recording-count
metric_types.label: Active Recording Count
metric_types.description: The recordings a component reports it has in progress now.

metric_types.name: queue-depth
metric_types.label: Queue Depth
metric_types.description: The items a component reports waiting in its work queue, not yet picked up.

metric_types.name: http-response-time
metric_types.label: HTTP Response Time
metric_types.description: Time for the probe's HTTP request to draw a response (any status); absent when the API never answered.

metric_types.name: ssh-handshake-time
metric_types.label: SSH Handshake Time
metric_types.description: Time for the SSH key exchange to reach authentication; absent when the daemon never completed it.

metric_types.name: telnet-response-time
metric_types.label: Telnet Response Time
metric_types.description: Time for a telnet port to send its first bytes (an option negotiation or a banner) after the connection opened; absent when the port accepted and stayed silent.

metric_types.name: tls-handshake-time
metric_types.label: TLS Handshake Time
metric_types.description: Time for the TLS handshake to reach the certificate after the connection opened, one observation per probe the component answered; absent when it never answered the handshake.

metric_types.name: udp-response-time
metric_types.label: UDP Response Time
metric_types.description: Time for a udp endpoint's request rung to be answered, from its first send, so a lost datagram's retry shows as time; one observation per probe the component answered, absent when every attempt was lost.

metric_types.name: snmp-response-time
metric_types.label: SNMP Response Time
metric_types.description: Time for an snmp endpoint's request rung, a get of a standard OID, to be answered, one observation per probe the agent answered (an authorizationError included); absent when the get went unanswered.

metric_types.name: tls-certificate-days-left
metric_types.label: TLS Certificate Days Left
metric_types.description: Days from the probe to the not-after of the certificate a tls probe accepted, to the hundredth, negative once it has expired; one observation per probe, the number a threshold rule reads (an expression cannot read the clock).

event_types.name: call-started
event_types.label: Call Started
event_types.description: A conferencing endpoint entered an active call. A caught occurrence when the device reports it natively (an xAPI event), or a derived one when a rule infers it from other signals.

event_types.name: command-issued
event_types.label: Command Issued
event_types.description: A command was issued to a component (the caused event a command records). It opens the intended value the command sets and is the lineage cause of that intended value.

event_types.name: command-settled
event_types.label: Command Settled
event_types.description: A command took effect: its reply confirmed it or carried the intended value, or an observation of its target matched. Its message says which, and the command row keeps the evidence.

event_types.name: command-failed
event_types.label: Command Failed
event_types.description: A command did not take effect: its execution failed, its reply contradicted it, or the value observed when its settle window closed was another. Its message gives the reason.

event_types.name: command-timed-out
event_types.label: Command Timed Out
event_types.description: A command's settle window closed with no evidence either way: no reply that decided it and no observation of its target. Its message says where it stopped (never taken by a node, delivered with no report, or answered with nothing observed after).

event_types.name: call-ended
event_types.label: Call Ended
event_types.description: A conferencing endpoint left an active call: call-started's closing half, caught natively or derived. The pair brackets a session for usage reads.

event_types.name: input-changed
event_types.label: Input Changed
event_types.description: A display or switcher moved to a different source input. Caught natively where the device reports it; a frequent, benign occurrence that teaches the event lane's volume without implying a fault.

event_types.name: recording-failed
event_types.label: Recording Failed
event_types.description: A recording service could not complete a recording. Caught natively where the service reports it; its payload names the recording and why it failed.

event_types.name: collection-failed
event_types.label: Collection Failed
event_types.description: A collection task could not use what it had: an unusable config or a payload that did not parse. Carries the task identity in its payload, so the failure names its work; the alternative is a silent skip nobody sees.

event_types.name: condition-started
event_types.label: Condition Started
event_types.description: An event rule's condition came into force on a component: the generic fire event for a rule that needs no semantic type of its own. Written once at the edge, after the rule's fire sustain, never per sample while the condition holds.

event_types.name: condition-ended
event_types.label: Condition Ended
event_types.description: An event rule's condition left force: condition-started's closing half, written once when the rule's clear criteria has held for its clear sustain. The pair brackets how long the condition held.

command_types.name: set-input
command_types.label: Set Input
command_types.description: Tell a display or switcher which video input to select. A settleable command: it opens an intended video-input and settles when the device reports that input within the settle window.

command_types.name: reboot
command_types.label: Reboot
command_types.description: Tell a component to restart. A fire-and-forget command: it opens no intended value, so its node's execution report settles or fails it, and it times out when no report arrives within its delivery window. A disruptive one: its delivery closes the gates of its hold set on that node (the component's in-band endpoints and those of what it hosts), the node runs nothing against them for the quiet period, then each reopens on its own first up verdict, with the hold as the backstop for one that never reads up.

command_types.name: outlet-off
command_types.label: Outlet Off
command_types.description: Switch one outlet of a PDU off. A fire-and-forget command and a power command: its delivery closes the gates of what that outlet feeds on the node (every endpoint of a component with a power dependency on the outlet, its out-of-band ones included, and the in-band endpoints of what those host), never the PDU's own, so the node sends nothing to a component while its power is cut. Each reopens on its own first up verdict after the quiet period, with the hold as the backstop for one that stays dark.

command_types.name: outlet-on
command_types.label: Outlet On
command_types.description: Switch one outlet of a PDU on. A fire-and-forget command that disrupts nothing: restoring power holds no gate, and what the outlet feeds reads up again on its own probes as it boots.

command_types.name: set-volume
command_types.label: Set Volume
command_types.description: Tell a component its output volume, as a percentage. A settleable command: it opens an intended volume and settles when the component reports it, or when its reply confirms the change.

command_types.name: set-mute
command_types.label: Set Mute
command_types.description: Tell a component to mute ("true") or unmute ("false") its audio. A settleable command against the mute state.

command_types.name: set-power
command_types.label: Set Power
command_types.description: Tell a component to turn on, turn off, or enter standby. A settleable command against the power state.

notification_types.name: alarm-raised
notification_types.label: Alarm raised
notification_types.description: Says an alarm opened: what is wrong, where, and how bad. The message an action rule on raised sends unless it names another type.
notification_types.subject: [{{.SeverityLabel}}] {{.ComponentLabel}}: {{.Message}}

notification_types.name: alarm-cleared
notification_types.label: Alarm cleared
notification_types.description: Says an alarm closed, so whoever was told it opened is told it is over. The message an action rule on cleared sends unless it names another type.
notification_types.subject: [Cleared] {{.ComponentLabel}}: {{.Message}}

transports.name: icmp
transports.description: ICMP echo / ping reachability and RTT.

transports.name: tcp
transports.description: Raw TCP: the connect / port-open check, and the line protocol, which holds a session over it (polls, commands, and listeners share one connection).

transports.name: tls
transports.description: TLS: the line protocol over a TLS connection, held exactly as it is over tcp; the probe runs the handshake (responds) and reports the certificate's expiry, verified against the node's roots, pinned to the public key on first use, or (by the operator's explicit choice) not verified.

transports.name: udp
transports.description: UDP: the line protocol as datagrams, one line each, stateless: the probe sends the driver's named request and an answer is the rung (an open udp port cannot be detected), a refused port reads refused, and a lost datagram is retried; each endpoint binds its own local port (its driver's listen-port input, else one the node picks), which its requests, replies and pushes share.

transports.name: telnet
transports.description: Telnet: the line protocol over TCP with option negotiation (every option refused), its login the session's auth step; the probe connects and waits for the first negotiation or banner bytes (responds).

transports.name: ssh
transports.description: SSH: the probe runs a real key exchange (responds) and tries the endpoint credential when one is set (auth); the line protocol holds a shell or exec channel over it, its userauth the session's auth step and its host key pinned on first use.

transports.name: http
transports.description: HTTP: a driver's polls and commands send real requests (method, path, query, headers, body) and read JSON, XML, HTML or text answers, authenticated by the endpoint's declared scheme (basic, bearer, an API key, digest) or a login whose session the node keeps; a declared server-sent events stream is held as a session, its events landing through the listeners; the probe draws a real response off the API without a credential (responds), any status counting as an answer.

transports.name: https
transports.description: HTTPS: http over a TLS connection, its own entry so a component can serve a plain web port beside a TLS one, a server-sent events stream held over it as over http; the probe runs the handshake (responds), reports the certificate's expiry, then draws a response, the certificate verified against the node's roots, pinned to the public key on first use, or (by the operator's explicit choice) not verified.

transports.name: websocket
transports.description: WebSocket: a held session whose messages are text frames, routed as a line session's are: a frame sent to arm a subscription on every connection, pushes landing through the listeners, and a request answered by the frame carrying back an id the node mints into it, whatever pushes interleave; the upgrade rides the endpoint's scheme (basic, bearer, an API key) or a login whose cookie the node keeps, and the session is kept alive by ping and pong; the probe is http's, a credential-free GET / whose answer, any status, is the rung (responds), so reachability stays observed beneath a refused upgrade.

transports.name: wss
transports.description: WSS: websocket over a TLS connection, its own entry so a component can serve a plain socket beside a TLS one; the probe is https's: it runs the handshake (responds), reports the certificate's expiry, then draws a credential-free response, the certificate verified against the node's roots, pinned to the public key on first use, or (by the operator's explicit choice) not verified.

transports.name: snmp
transports.description: SNMP v2c, stateless: the probe gets a standard OID (sysUpTime.0 unless the driver names another) with the endpoint's community, and an answer is the rung; a wrong community is dropped silently and reads as no answer, while an authorizationError reads as an auth refusal.

transports.name: webhook
transports.description: Webhook: a push transport the server hosts, not one a node dials: a component or a cloud service posts each message to the endpoint's own URL (/api/v1/webhooks/ and a token the server mints, held as a secret), authenticated by the scheme its driver declares (an hmac signature over a signed timestamp, a token, basic, or none, which reads unsigned) and mapped by its listeners onto any lane; nothing is dialed, so it has no reachability ladder and reads last heard.
